pr_title: topsql: fix issue of topsql failed catch the running SQL when topsql is enabled in execution
pr_body:
<!--

Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:
1. pkg [, pkg2, pkg3]: what's changed
2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?
<!--

Please create an issue first to describe the problem.

There MUST be one line starting with "Issue Number:  " and 
linking the relevant issues via the "close" or "ref".

For more info, check https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/contribute-code.html#referring-to-an-issue.

-->

Issue Number: close #33859

Problem Summary:

Fix issue of topsql failed catch the running SQL when topsql is enabled in execution

### What is changed and how it works?

Always attach the SQL and Plan information whether TopSQL is enabled.

### Benchmark Test

#### Sysbench test

Machine:  AWS c4.4xlarge, 16 cpu core, 32G memory.
Topology: 1*TiDB, 1*TiKV, 1*PD

Disable TopSQL(threads=300) | QPS in This PR | QPS in Master | Impact(%)
-- | -- | -- | --
Point-Get | 37396 | 37642 | 0.6535253175
Read-Only | 19108 | 19343 | 1.214909786



Enable TopSQL(threads=300) | QPS in This PR | QPS in Master | Impact(%)
-- | -- | -- | --
Point-Get | 34671 | 34643 | -0.08082440897
Read-Only | 17701 | 17682 | -0.1074539079



### Check List

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- [ ] Unit test
- [x] Integration test
- [x] Manual test (add detailed scripts or steps below)

1. Create table `t1` and insert into 10000000 rows data.

2. Mock some normal OLTP load by [loadgen](https://github.com/crazycs520/loadgen):

```shell
bin/loadgen payload normal-oltp --rows=1000000
```

3. Execute following SQLs in client-A and client-B at same:

```sql
select count(*),sum(a+b),sum(b+d),sum(c+d*2), sum(d*2+a*b), avg(a*b*d), avg(b*c), avg(c*d),avg(a*b*d), avg(2*b*c), avg(3*c*d), sum(a*b*c), sum(b*d) from t1;
```

```sql
select count(*) from t1 as t0 join t1 as t1 on t0.a != t1.a;
```

4. enable TopSQL during the upper SQL execution:

```sql
set @@global.tidb_enable_top_sql=1;
```

5. Check the TopSQL data.

TiDB: 

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26020263/162688286-822ba4ff-39c9-45ae-8aca-d25ddc023bcd.png)

TiKV

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/26020263/162688436-2b43d410-b7bb-4242-a30f-4c30055332d5.png)


Side effects

- [x] Performance regression: Consumes more CPU

### Release note

<!-- compatibility change, improvement, bugfix, and new feature need a release note -->

Please refer to [Release Notes Language Style Guide](https://pingcap.github.io/tidb-dev-guide/contribute-to-tidb/release-notes-style-guide.html) to write a quality release note.

```release-note
Fix issue of TopSQL failed to catch the running SQL when TopSQL is enabled in execution.
```

issue_context.title: topsql failed catch the running SQL when Top SQL is enabled in execution
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

### 1. Minimal reproduce step (Required)

1. Create table `t1` and insert into 10000000 rows data.
2. Execute following SQLs in client-A and client-B at same time:

```sql
select count(*),sum(a+b),sum(b+d),sum(c+d*2), sum(d*2+a*b), avg(a*b*d), avg(b*c), avg(c*d),avg(a*b*d), avg(2*b*c), avg(3*c*d), sum(a*b*c), sum(b*d) from t1;
```

```sql
select count(*) from t1 as t0 join t1 as t1 on t0.a != t1.a;
```

3. enable TopSQL during the upper SQL execution:

```sql
set @@global.tidb_enable_top_sql=1;
```

### 2. What did you expect to see? (Required)

TopSQL should catch the running SQL when Top SQL is enabled in execution.

### 3. What did you see instead (Required)

topsql failed catch the running SQL when Top SQL is enabled in execution.

### 4. What is your TiDB version? (Required)

<!-- Paste the output of SELECT tidb_version() -->

```sql
0d7602eb6551c9a53732be4da37d6ac2f22e375d (HEAD -> master, origin/master)
```

review_comments:
I'm not sure, but the relationship looks wired. Could you confirm are there better paths?

The current path is:

ExecStatement -> SessionVars -> StatementCtx -> IsSQLRegistered

So, for example, is it possible to be:

ExecStatement -> IsSQLRegistered?
explanation/comment needed
Why `linkSQLTextWithDigest` is called in `AttachSQLInfo` but is not called in `AttachSQLAndPlanInfo`?

Maybe rename the function `AttachSQLInfo ` to `AttachAndRegisterSQLInfo` is better.

Since when topsql is disabled, when calling `AttachSQLAndPlanInfo` but not register SQL/Plan info for getting better performance.
why enable topsql in such a complicated way?
Any advice? Since I need to enable topsql when the SQL in execution.
Our propose is to catch requests that is not tagged. How about bypassing the Top SQL layer at all and only check these request tags?

This PR propose is to catch the running SQL when topsql is enabled in execution.
Check request not tagged is already checked by https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/pull/33623

Note (no need to change in this PR): a better API design should be a hook framework for statement begin and statement finish events, instead of something xxxForTopSQL. (The observer pattern)

cc @mornyx @zhongzc
`OnExecutionBegin` will be skipped executed after this return?
Yes, since it has a performance impact when TopSQL is disabled.
Looks like there are potential performance improvements here @mornyx @zhongzc
In my sysbench point-get test, `OnExecutionBegin` and `OnExecutionFinished` have around %3 QPS impact.

By the way, when TopSQL is enabled, I think the overhead of `OnExecutionBegin()` is mostly about **lock**. I think we can consider learning `nanolog`'s lock-free-buffer pattern to optimize performance here. cc @zhongzc
How about let's shard the lock into N? It should be very easy to implement and effectively enough to verify the lock cost.

> How about let's shard the lock into N? It should be very easy to implement and effectively enough to verify the lock cost.

Can do a test, I think it will work. Since the session is serial, the only scenario where lock contention occurs is the collection of background goroutine. So in theory, segmented locks can effectively reduce the possibility of sessions being blocked by background goroutine.
Not from lock. I tried to remove all locks previously and found the performance impact was not reduced much.

> Not from lock. I tried to remove all locks previously and found the performance impact was not reduced much.

This seems a bit strange, the logic of `OnExecutionBegin` is very simple (get an item from the map, then increment it). This shouldn't cause a 3% QPS regression... cc @crazycs520
map-assign and map-access have become the main cause. A more complicated lock implementation will introduce extra overhead and worse performance.
why would a single map-assign and access cause this kind of drop? It doesn't make sense.
Will it happen that `IsSQLAndPlanRegistered == true` while `IsSQLRegistered == false`?
It will happen, but it doesn't matter, the code can make sure if `IsSQLAndPlanRegistered ` is true, then the `SQL` and `plan` must be registerd.
duplicated with RegisterSQL?
No, if this function is called, then `RegisterSQL` won't be call anymore.
